title: Arterial Blood Gas — Pattern Recognition
prompt: A 24-year-old presents with deep, rapid breathing and altered mental status after several days of polyuria and thirst. The arterial blood gas below is drawn on room air. Mark every value that is outside its reference range, then choose the best interpretation of the overall pattern.

choices.feedback: The low pH (acidemia) rules out alkalosis as the primary disturbance.

choices.text: High anion gap metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation
choices.feedback: Correct. Low pH + low HCO₃⁻ indicate metabolic acidosis; the elevated anion gap (28) and the low PaCO₂ (respiratory compensation, Winters' formula) fit. Clinical picture suggests diabetic ketoacidosis.
The anion gap here is 28 — well above the 8–12 reference — so this is a high-gap, not normal-gap, acidosis.
PaCO₂ is decreased, not increased, so there is no respiratory acidosis. The hypocapnia represents respiratory compensation.

overallFeedback.message: Review acid–base diagnosis: start with pH, then HCO₃⁻ and PaCO₂, then the gap.
Close — re-check whether each value lies in its reference range.
All abnormalities flagged and pattern correctly identified.
